findings.claim: Step 2 says to take only candidates whose title matches the request, but never defines 'matches'. Duplicate detection also depends on body content, so title-only filtering can drop real duplicates. The 10 bound is applied after the filter, so a search with many body-only matches silently reads none of them. The stop on more than 10 gives no instruction on what 'asks the owner' should offer.
proof_refs: skills/issue-creation/references/procedure.md:10 'take only the candidates whose title matches the request, at most 10'

findings.claim: The normalization rule says to drop trailing white space at the end of each line and of the text, but does not say whether leading or trailing blank lines or a final newline are covered. 'Trailing white space at the end of the text' is ambiguous for a trailing newline, so two readers could reach different equal/unknown outcomes. Also, it does not state that the same normalization applies to the title.
proof_refs: skills/issue-creation/references/procedure.md:17 'dropping trailing white space at the end of each line and of the text'

findings.claim: The unknown outcome for a missing or unparsable URL is stated only in step 5. The comment case, where gh issue comment prints a URL without an #issuecomment- fragment, is covered only implicitly. The Read-back comparison section, which lists the unknown conditions, was not updated to mention it, so the two places can drift.

evidence: Only skills/issue-creation/references/procedure.md changed; the diff modifies steps 2 and 5 and the Read-back comparison paragraph.
Findings are about ambiguity introduced by the new wording; no behavioral regression is demonstrable from the diff alone.
